title: lodash `_.template` — Open-Source Profile Assessment (Dogfood Run 2)
description: Second dogfood run for INIT-THREATMODELSPEC-002 (RMI-THREATMODELSPEC-117): a real third-party open-source dependency (lodash, https://github.com/lodash/lodash) analyzed under the 'open-source' artifact-availability profile — public documentation and source code only, no telemetry or deployment visibility. Grounded in CVE-2021-23337 (GitHub Advisory GHSA-35jh-r3h4-6jhm), a real, publicly disclosed and patched command-injection vulnerability in lodash's `_.template` function, verified via WebFetch against the live GitHub Advisory Database and lodash's own README/docs during this analysis.

authors.name: product-definition-analyst, builder-definition-analyst, implementation-analyst (tms analyze dogfood run 2, open-source profile)

diagrams.title: Downstream Consumer Using lodash _.template
diagrams.description: How a downstream application's use of lodash's _.template function processes potentially untrusted input.

elements.label: External / User-Controlled Input
elements.description: Content that could reach a downstream application's template rendering path (form input, uploaded content, etc.).

elements.label: Downstream Consumer Application
elements.description: Any Node.js application that depends on lodash and calls _.template — outside the scope of what lodash itself controls.

elements.label: lodash _.template()
elements.description: Compiles a template string into a JS function using configurable escape/evaluate/interpolate delimiters and a templateSettings.variable/sourceURL option set.

elements.label: Application Process (Node.js runtime)
elements.description: The execution context compromised if template compilation evaluates attacker-controlled code.

threatActors.name: Attacker able to influence content reaching a downstream app's template pipeline
threatActors.description: CVE-2021-23337 is a publicly disclosed, well-documented vulnerability with known exploitation patterns — low sophistication is sufficient once a downstream app is found to pass untrusted input into _.template.
primaryGoals: Achieve remote code/command execution in a downstream application that uses vulnerable lodash versions

mitigations.title: Upgrade to lodash >= 4.17.21 and never construct _.template's options/source from untrusted input
mitigations.description: Per the GitHub Advisory, lodash 4.17.21 contains the fix for CVE-2021-23337. Independent of the version fix, downstream callers should never pass user-controlled data as the template source string or the templateSettings/options object; if user data must appear in output, it must only ever flow through the interpolate delimiter as data, never as part of the template source or evaluate-delimited code.

assets.name: Downstream application process execution context
assets.description: The Node.js process of any application that depends on lodash and calls _.template — not an asset lodash itself holds data in, but one whose integrity depends on how lodash's template compilation behaves.
assets.value: Full compromise (arbitrary command execution) if template compilation evaluates attacker-controlled input, per CVE-2021-23337.

scenarios.title: Command injection via lodash _.template (CVE-2021-23337)
preconditions: Downstream application passes user-influenced content into _.template's string or options argument
attackPath: Attacker identifies a downstream application feature that renders user content through lodash's _.template
Attacker crafts input exploiting the template compilation's evaluate/sourceURL handling to inject executable code
The compiled template function executes the injected code with the downstream application's own privileges
scenarios.outcome: Arbitrary command/code execution within the downstream application's Node.js process.
scenarios.businessImpact: A single vulnerable transitive dependency (lodash < 4.17.21) can grant full remote code execution in any consuming application that reaches the vulnerable code path — the real-world supply-chain risk this repo's own supply-chain-vulnerable-dependency.json example was built to represent.

evidence.excerpt: A modern JavaScript utility library delivering modularity, performance, & extras.
evidence.summary: lodash's own README describes it as a general-purpose utility library — iterating arrays/objects/strings, manipulating/testing values, creating composite functions. No stated scope around executing untrusted input as code.

evidence.excerpt: Lodash versions prior to 4.17.21 are vulnerable to Command Injection via the template function.
evidence.summary: GitHub Advisory Database entry for CVE-2021-23337 (CVSS 7.2, High): command injection via lodash's template function, affecting npm lodash < 4.17.21, fixed in 4.17.21. Verified live via WebFetch during this analysis run.

evidence.excerpt: _.templateSettings: escape (pattern for escaped text), evaluate (pattern for code evaluation), interpolate (pattern for variable interpolation), variable (variable name for template data), imports._ (methods available within templates).
evidence.summary: lodash's own documentation confirms _.template's evaluate delimiter exists specifically to embed and execute JavaScript inside a compiled template — the exact mechanism CVE-2021-23337 abuses when an options object is built from untrusted input.

evidence.excerpt: (source-tree fetch attempted; template() function not reached before tool summarization truncated the file)
evidence.summary: The open-source profile grants source-tree access in principle, but this run's read-only web-fetch tooling summarized/truncated lodash.js before reaching the template() function, so no direct file+line citation for the vulnerable code path was obtained in this run. This is a real limitation of the tooling used, not of the profile or the vulnerability's confirmed existence (CVE-2021-23337 is independently confirmed via evidence-ghsa-35jh from the product-definition stage) — recorded honestly rather than fabricating a line citation.

securityRequirements.statement: The _.template function must never evaluate attacker-controlled input as executable JavaScript when invoked with default or documented options, regardless of what options object a downstream caller constructs.

architectureAssertions.expected: mitigation-upgrade-and-never-pass-untrusted-options (builder-definition stage) is verifiable against the actual source: either the dependency is pinned >= 4.17.21, or no call site passes untrusted data into template()'s source/options.
architectureAssertions.observed: Not verified in this run — see evidence-lodash-source-fetch-attempt. A real static-analysis pass over a cloned source tree (not attempted here) would be needed to check this for real, not just cite the advisory.

findings.title: _.template's evaluate/sourceURL/variable options are a code-execution trust boundary with no built-in caller-side guardrail
findings.description: The boundary crossed here is: 'external-input' -> 'downstream-app' -> 'lodash-template' (per this run's DFD). lodash's own documentation confirms the evaluate delimiter's purpose is to embed and execute arbitrary JS in the compiled template. Nothing in the documented API prevents a caller from constructing that options object (or the template string itself) from unsanitized external input — the library provides the capability, the calling application owns the trust decision entirely. CVE-2021-23337 is exactly this boundary being crossed carelessly by callers.

findings.title: lodash < 4.17.21 template() is vulnerable to command injection (CVE-2021-23337)
findings.description: Confirmed via the GitHub Advisory Database (GHSA-35jh-r3h4-6jhm, evidence-ghsa-35jh from the product-definition stage): lodash versions prior to 4.17.21 are vulnerable to command injection via the template function, CVSS 7.2 (High), fixed in 4.17.21. This finding is recorded at implementation-stage confidence (not merely a design-level candidate) because the CVE is a publicly disclosed, third-party-confirmed, already-patched vulnerability — not a hypothesis requiring further validation.
